h: "So That Your Generations May Know": The Season of Our Rejoicing

p: This festival is called "the Season of our Rejoicing,"
for it is written, "In sukkos you shall dwell," etc.,
that I made the Children of Yisrael
And they asked: why was no remembrance made
for the manna and the well,
but only for the Clouds of Glory?
But in truth one must look closely:
if the reason for the sukkah
is a remembrance of the Clouds of Glory,
"so that you remember that in sukkos," etc.,
the day of your going out from the land of Egypt"
Yet it is written, "so that they may know,"
meaning that the knowledge should enter the heart
And this is as we find with Yaakov
on account of "for you have striven
with God and with men, and have prevailed"
That is, at first he was in fear
who is Samael, the evil inclination,
and who appeared to him as a Torah scholar
he touched the hollow of his thigh,
for he still had a claim.
when there was no longer any accusation against him;
then it is written, "And Yaakov journeyed to Sukkos
for Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
was truly made complete in every respect,
as it says, "You will grant truth to Yaakov"
"The lip of truth shall be established forever"
that is, for his children and his descendants,
as we find in the Midrash
that Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, had
and the number six hundred thousand
is the number of the roots of the souls of Yisrael,
and for this reason they are called "his cattle."
so that at the very least they would merit
And this is the protection from the evil inclination,
"And a sukkah shall be for shade by day," etc.
and it is brought in the Raya Mehemna
"And not in the shade of an ordinary sukkah
that shields the body from the sun,
but a shade to shield the soul."
And this is what it says, "from storm and from rain,"
"He will rain snares upon the wicked"
that is, from all the sins,
as it is written, "And the goat shall bear
'their iniquities' (avonosam) — the iniquities of the wholesome one (tam)."
After this a sukkah is needed
and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He,
helps him, he could not overcome it.
as it is written, "Light is sown for the righteous"
as it is written, "and for the upright in heart, joy" (ibid.).
a mighty man who conquers his inclination,
and he needs light to shine for him
he still has a struggle and a war,
and he is not in joy.
one who merits to straighten the heart,
לְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל גַּם כֵּן,
to empty the evil from the "heart of the fool" as well —
And Yaakov merited uprightness of heart
and Yisrael merit it at least
during the days of the festival of Sukkos.
And this is the attribute of da'as,
"He made Yaakov in the mystery of da'as."
And this is what Yisrael merit on Sukkos:
that they merit the attribute of da'as,
"for I made them dwell in sukkos":
And therefore the festival is called "the Season of our Rejoicing."
"Just as the Holy One, blessed be He,
on these days and rejoices in them,
the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion
For Hashem, may He be blessed, rejoices with Yisrael
for this was the purpose of creation,
לֹא בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ
"The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world
only so that people would fear Him,
as it says, 'And God has made it so
And at the end of the sixth chapter of Avos (Mishnah 11):
כָּל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
"Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created
in His world, He created only for His glory."
That is, that the attribute of His Kingship be revealed:
"a king whose awe is upon you"
and Hashem, may He be blessed, has joy
And Yisrael, when they merit uprightness of heart:
whoever is of the holy root
from the war of the evil inclination,
and they rejoice with Hashem, may He be blessed:
And the festival is called "the Season of our Rejoicing."

inlineHeadings.text: Why a remembrance of the clouds alone?
"So that they may know": knowledge, not memory
Yaakov named Yisrael and the hollow of the thigh
A sukkah to shield from the yetzer
A sukkah to shield the soul
"Light for the righteous, joy for the upright"
Yaakov's uprightness: the attribute of da'as
All was created for His glory
"Every native in Yisrael shall dwell in sukkos"

paragraphs.text: Commentary: Rashi on Vayikra 23:43 — “‘That I made [the Children of Israel] dwell in sukkos’: the Clouds of Glory (Sukkah 11b; Mechilta 12).” Connection: Rashi takes the sukkos of the verse to be the Clouds of Glory, the reading behind the maamar's question of why the sukkah commemorates the clouds and not the manna or the well.

paragraphs.text: Chullin 91a — “Rav Shmuel bar Acha said before Rav Pappa in Rava bar Ulla's name: He appeared to him as a Torah scholar, for the Master said: One who walks at his teacher's right is an uncultivated person.” The discussion asks how Yaakov's assailant stood relative to him. One view says he appeared as a gentile; this view says he appeared as a Torah scholar. Rav Tzadok applies that disguise to evil counsel that presents itself as religious instruction.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52b — "Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says, 'The wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to kill him' (Tehillim 37:32); and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not overcome it, as it says, 'Hashem will not abandon him into his hand' (Tehillim 37:33)."

paragraphs.text: Taanis 15a — "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say: not all are for light and not all are for gladness. The righteous are for light, and the upright for gladness: the righteous for light, as it is written, 'Light is sown for the righteous' (Tehillim 97:11); and the upright for gladness, as it is written, 'and for the upright of heart, gladness.'"

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 14b–15a (Shemos) — "The world was created with three: with wisdom, with understanding and with knowledge (Shemos 31:3)... When He wished to establish the world, He made Avraham in the secret of Chochmah, Yitzchak in the secret of Tevunah, and Yaakov in the secret of Da'as; thus it is called 'and with da'as the chambers are filled' (Mishlei 24:4)."

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 31b — "Rav Yehudah said: The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world only so that they should fear Him, as it says, 'And God has made it so, that they should fear before Him' (Koheles 3:14)."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shemini 3 — “But the matter is according to what they said (Shabbos 31b): the Holy One, blessed be He, created His world only so that they would fear Him, as it says, ‘And God has made it so that they fear Him’ (Koheles 3:14).” Connection: Both bring Koheles 3:14 on fear of Heaven as the purpose of creation.

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 32b — "Rav Ashi said: Even according to the one who says that a nasi who forgoes his honor, his honor is forgone — a king who forgoes his honor, his honor is not forgone, as it says, 'You shall surely set a king over you' (Devarim 17:15): that his awe be upon you."

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 103a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Emor) — "'In sukkos you shall dwell seven days' (Vayikra 23:42): this commandment is to dwell in the sukkah… to show that Israel dwell in the secret of faith without any fear, for the accuser has departed from them. And whoever is in the secret of faith sits in the sukkah, as it is written, 'Every native in Israel shall dwell in sukkos' — whoever is of the secret of faith, of the seed and root of Israel, shall dwell in sukkos."
